common_name: Cherries Jubilee Heuchera (Bronze-Purple Coral Bells with Cherry-Red Flowers)

planting.note: Plant container divisions in spring in humus-rich, well-drained soil in partial shade; Cherries Jubilee is a Terra Nova introduction bred from Heuchera sanguinea for its unusually vivid, long-lasting flower color.

directions: Plant in humus-rich, well-drained soil in partial shade with morning sun and afternoon shelter, since strong afternoon exposure fades the dusty bronze-purple leaf color. Cherries Jubilee is grown as much for its flowers as its foliage, sending up fuzzy 16-inch scapes of bright cherry-red bells well above the ruffled, upward-curling leaves whose undersides flash red-purple. Deadhead spent scapes to encourage repeat flushes through summer, and divide congested clumps every three to four years in spring to maintain vigor. Consistent moisture and sharp drainage together matter more than either alone, since crowns rot quickly in soggy sites.

common_name: Fire Chief Heuchera (Reblooming Scarlet-Leaved Coral Bells)

planting.note: Plant container divisions in spring in humus-rich, well-drained soil in partial to full shade; Fire Chief is a Terra Nova introduction selected for reblooming flowers and season-long scarlet foliage with good powdery mildew resistance.

directions: Plant in humus-rich, well-drained soil in partial to full shade; Fire Chief holds its glowing wine-red to crimson leaf color through the season better than many older red-leaved heucheras, forming a tidy, low basal mound. Open sprays of small bicolor pink-and-white bells rise on dark red stems and rebloom repeatedly from early summer into fall if spent scapes are trimmed back. The cultivar shows better-than-average drought tolerance once established and resists powdery mildew, but still benefits from consistent moisture and sharp drainage to prevent crown rot. Divide congested clumps every three to four years in spring.
sources: North Carolina State Extension — Heuchera for Southern Gardens

common_name: Ring of Fire Heuchera (Silver Maple-Leaf Coral Bells with Dark Veins)

planting.note: Plant container divisions in spring in humus-rich, well-drained soil in partial to full shade; Ring of Fire is a Terra Nova hybrid selected for its silvery, maple-shaped leaves overlaid with contrasting dark veining.

directions: Plant in humus-rich, well-drained soil in partial to full shade; Ring of Fire's silvery, deeply lobed, maple-shaped leaves are traced with dark contrasting veins that read almost metallic in low shade light, making it a strong textural accent toward the front of a shaded border. Small pale flower spikes rise above the foliage in late spring but are secondary to the season-long foliage display. Provide steady moisture through summer heat and sharp drainage to prevent crown rot, and divide congested clumps every three to four years in spring to keep the mound tight and well-colored.
